title: Ensure all default accounts are either disabled or utilize strong passwords
description: Disable the known default accounts configured. Note: The default admin account must remain enabled for high availability synchronization to work. Disabling it could cause issues.
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.4 Ensure all default accounts are either disabled or utilize strong passwords

audit.command: In GUI: - Navigate to System > User Manager > Users - View the default users

remediation.command:
In GUI:
-
Navigate to System > User Manager > Users
- Remove any default users that are not used. Note: The default admin account must remain enabled for high availability synchronization to work. Disabling it could cause issues.

title: Ensure default password of admin is changed
description: To assist users in changing the default password for 'admin' account.
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.4 Ensure default password of admin is changed

audit.command: Try to login to the GUI with: Username: admin Password: pfsense

remediation.command:
In the GUI:
-
Navigate to System > User Manager
- CLIck the Pencil Icon under 'Actions'
- Change the password of the default 'admin' user account.
- CLIck 'Save' at the bottom of the page.

title: Ensure Web Management is Set to use HTTPS
description: Web Admin Management Portal should only be accessed using HTTPS Protocol. PASS requires <protocol>https</protocol> inside <system><webgui>. Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.8 Ensure Web Management is Set to use HTTPS

remediation.command:
GUI: System > Advanced > Admin Access > webConfigurator > Protocol = HTTPS (SSL/TLS), select a certificate, Save.
# CIS guidance:
In the GUI:
-
Navigate to System > Advanced > Admin Access
- Select 'HTTPS' in the 'webConfigurator'.
- CLIck 'Save'

title: Ensure LDAP or RADIUS server configured
description: Configured the LDAP Servers or Radius server for central authentication. PASS requires at least one LDAP or RADIUS authentication server. Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.2 Ensure LDAP or RADIUS server configured

remediation.command:
GUI: System > User Manager > Authentication Servers > Add: Type LDAP or RADIUS, fill in the server details, Save; then select it under System > User Manager > Settings.
# CIS guidance:
In the GUI:
-
Navigate to System > User Manager.
- CLIck the Authentication Servers at the top.
- Configure "Authentication Servers" Setting

title: Ensure Console Menu is Password Protected
description: Set the Console Menu to password protected. PASS requires 'Password protect the console menu' (<disableconsolemenu> present). Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.3 Ensure Console Menu is Password Protected

remediation.command:
GUI: System > Advanced > Admin Access > Console Options: tick Password protect the console menu, Save.
# CIS guidance:
In the GUI:
-
Navigate to System > Advanced > Admin Access.
- Set "Console Options" Setting
- CLIck "Save"

title: Ensure no Allow Rule with Any in Destination Field present in the Firewall Rules
description: The Firewall Rules with Any in Source field allows all the IP Addresses of the Network to access the specified destination configured in the Firewall rules for specific services. FAILs if any pass rule in config.xml has destination any (disabled rules and the default LAN allow-any rule are also flagged, as the CIS default notes). Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 4.1.1 Ensure no Allow Rule with Any in Destination Field present in the Firewall Rules

remediation.command:
GUI: Firewall > Rules > <interface>: edit each pass rule with Destination any and set a specific host/network alias, or disable/delete it, Apply Changes.
# CIS guidance:
Delete or Disable the rule from the firewall which has Any used in the Destination field.

title: Ensure no Allow Rule with Any in Source field present in the Firewall Rules
description: The Firewall Rules with Any in the Destination field allows accessing all the IP Addresses of Network from specified Sources configured in the Firewall rules for specific services FAILs if any pass rule in config.xml has source any (disabled rules are also flagged). Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 4.1.2 Ensure no Allow Rule with Any in Source field present in the Firewall Rules

remediation.command:
GUI: Firewall > Rules > <interface>: edit each pass rule with Source any and set a specific host/network alias, or disable/delete it, Apply Changes.
# CIS guidance:
Delete the rule from the firewall which has Any used in the Source field.

title: Ensure no Allow Rule with Any in Services field present in the Firewall Rules
description: The Firewall Rules with Any in the Service field allows accessing all the Services from specified Source to specified Destination configured in the Firewall rules.
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 4.1.3 Ensure no Allow Rule with Any in Services field present in the Firewall Rules

audit.command: Verify there are no allowed rules present in the firewall which has Any used in the Service field. In CLI: pfctl -sr

remediation.command: Delete the rule from the firewall which has Any used in the Service field.

title: Ensure RADIUS or LDAP are being used for VPN Authentication
description: Set backed authentication for VPN User to LDAP server. Configured the LDAP Servers server for central authentication.
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.4.1 Ensure RADIUS or LDAP are being used for VPN Authentication

audit.command: In the GUI: - Navigate to System > User Manager. - CLIck the Authentication Servers at the top. - Check 'Authentication Servers' Setting

remediation.command:
In the GUI:
-
Navigate to System > User Manager.
- CLIck the Authentication Servers at the top.
- Configure 'Authentication Servers' Setting

title: Ensure that OpenVPN is configured to use TLS encryption for secure communications.
description: Configure OpenVPN to use TLS encryption for secure communication with clients and servers.
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.4.3 Ensure that OpenVPN is configured to use TLS encryption for secure communications.

audit.command: VPN > OpenVPN > Servers > edit each server > Cryptographic Settings: confirm TLS Configuration ('Use a TLS Key') is enabled with TLS authentication or encryption and a generated key, and that the key direction and digest are set appropriately.

remediation.command:
In GUI Open the pfSense web interface and navigate to VPN > OpenVPN. CLIck on the server configuration you want to configure. Under the "Cryptographic Settings" section, set the "TLS Configuration" option to "Enable". Choose the appropriate TLS key length, key direction, and digest algorithm. CLIck "Save" to save the changes.
5.5 OpenVPN

title: Ensure SSH, when enabled, accepts public key authentication only
description: FAILs when the <ssh> block has <enable>enabled</enable> and sshdkeyonly is absent or set to 'both' (password or key). Passes when SSH is disabled. Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark - Secure Shell - SSHd Key Only (verify section number for your pfSense release)

remediation.command: GUI: System > Advanced > Admin Access > Secure Shell > SSHd Key Only = Public Key Only (add keys under System > User Manager first), Save. Or clear Enable Secure Shell.

title: Ensure IPv6 is disabled if not used
description: Although IPv6 has many advantages over IPv4, not all organizations have IPv6 or dual stack configurations implemented. FAILs if Allow IPv6 is enabled (<ipv6allow> present); document an exception if IPv6 is used. Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.6 Ensure IPv6 is disabled if not used

remediation.command:
GUI: System > Advanced > Networking: clear Allow IPv6, Save.
# CIS guidance:
In the CLI:
Add below in the '/etc/sysctl.conf' file and reboot.
- net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1
- net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=1
- net.ipv6.conf.lo.disable_ipv6 = 1 In the GUI:
Navigate to System > Advanced > Networking Uncheck 'Allow IPv6'

title: Ensure 'DNS Rebind Check' is unchecked
description: Ensure that the 'DNS Rebind Check' feature is unchecked to protect against DNS rebinding attacks. FAILs when 'Disable DNS Rebinding Checks' is ticked (<nodnsrebindcheck> present); the CIS title means this box must stay unchecked. Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.7 Ensure 'DNS Rebind Check' is unchecked

remediation.command:
GUI: System > Advanced > Admin Access: clear Disable DNS Rebinding Checks, Save.
# CIS guidance:
In the GUI
-
Navigate to System > Advance
- Uncheck on 'DNS Rebind Check' Field

title: Ensure a synchronized High Availability peer is configured
description: Ensure a High Availability peer is fully synchronized and in a passive or active state. PASS requires <hasync> with a non-empty Synchronize Config to IP. Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.9 Ensure a synchronized High Availability peer is configured

remediation.command:
GUI: System > High Avail. Sync: set Synchronize Config to IP, Remote System Username/Password and the sections to sync, Save.
# CIS guidance:
In the GUI:
-
Navigate to System > High Avail. Sync
- Setup each field and Hit Save

title: Ensure Sessions Timeout is set to less than or equal to 10 Minutes
description: The session inactivity timeout setting represents the amount of time a user can be inactive before the user's session times out and closes. It only affects user browser sessions. PASS requires <session_timeout> between 1 and 10 minutes (an empty value means the 240-minute default). Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1 Ensure Sessions Timeout is set to less than or equal to 10 Minutes

remediation.command:
GUI: System > User Manager > Settings > Session timeout = 10, Save.
# CIS guidance:
In GUI:
-
Navigate to System > User Manager
- CLIck the Setting at the top.
- set 10 in the 'Session Timeout' field.
- CLIck Save

title: Ensure 'Local Account status' is set to 'Disabled'
description: Disable the 'Local User' account except for the admin user.
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.1 Ensure 'Local Account status' is set to 'Disabled'

audit.command: Need to manually check each account.

remediation.command: Disabled Local User Account.

title: Ensure Login Protection Threshold is set to 30 or less
description: The Login Protection Threshold is a score-based system that helps to prevent unauthorized access to the pfSense firewall. This score is based on various criteria, including the number of unsuccessful login attempts from a specific IP address. This control ensures that the Login Protection Threshold is set to a value of 30 or less. PASS requires the Login Protection threshold (<sshguard_threshold>) between 1 and 30. Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.2 Ensure Login Protection Threshold is set to 30 or less

remediation.command:
GUI: System > Advanced > Admin Access > Login Protection > Threshold = 30, Save.
# CIS guidance:
In the GUI:
-
Navigate to System > Advanced
- Set 30 in the 'Login Protection' > 'Threshold' Field
- CLIck 'Save'

title: Ensure Allow access again after time is set to 300 or more second
description: Account password lockout >= 300 seconds. Allow access again after a user has been locked out (due to failed login attempts). The user is allowed access after the configured time if there have been no login attempts during that time). PASS requires the Login Protection blocktime (<sshguard_blocktime>) of 300 seconds or more. Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.3 Ensure Allow access again after time is set to 300 or more second

remediation.command:
GUI: System > Advanced > Admin Access > Login Protection > Blocktime = 300, Save.
# CIS guidance:
In GUI:
-
Navigate to System > Advanced > Admin Access
- set the 'Login Protection' options.
- set 'Blocktime' value to 300.
- CLIck Save

title: Ensure there are no Unused Policies
description: Ensure that there are no firewall policies that are unused
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 4.1.4 Ensure there are no Unused Policies

audit.command: Review all Firewall policies for use and validate the purpose of the policy.

remediation.command: Disable and then delete any unused firewall policies.

title: Ensure Logging is Enable for All Firewall Rules
description: Ensure all firewall rules have logging enable.
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 4.1.5 Ensure Logging is Enable for All Firewall Rules

audit.command: In the GUI: - Navigate to Status > System Logs > Settings - Verify Desired Logging Options are enabled

remediation.command:
In the GUI:
-
Navigate to Status > System Logs > Settings
- Check Desired Logging Options to enable.

title: Ensure ICMP Request is securely configured
description: ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol) is used by network devices to communicate with each other. While ICMP is essential for network management and troubleshooting, allowing all types of ICMP requests may increase the risk of attacks such as Ping Flood and ICMP Redirect. Therefore, it is recommended to securely configure the allowed types of ICMP requests on the firewall.
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 4.1.6 Ensure ICMP Request is securely configured

audit.command: In GUI: - Navigate to Firewall > Rules - Review the firewall rules to determine if any ICMP request rules are present. - Review the firewall rules to determine if any ICMP request rules are present. - Check the configured ICMP request types for each rule to ensure that only necessary types are allowed

remediation.command:
In GUI:
-
Navigate to Firewall > Rules
- Review the firewall rules to determine if any ICMP request rules are present.
- Review the firewall rules to determine if any ICMP request rules are present.
- Check the configured ICMP request types for each rule to ensure that only necessary types are allowed

title: Ensure SNMP traps receivers is set
description: Enables SNMP traps receivers where traps are sent. PASS requires a non-empty SNMP trap server in <snmpd>. Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.1.1 Ensure SNMP traps receivers is set

remediation.command:
GUI: Services > SNMP > SNMP Traps: tick Enable the SNMP Trap, set Trap server, port and string, Save.
# CIS guidance:
In GUI:
-
Navigate to Services > SNMP.
- Check "SNMP Traps Enable" is enable.
- Configured the "SNMP Trap Settings" value.
- CLIck Save

title: Ensure SNMP traps is enabled
description: Enables SNMP traps to be sent to the Network Management Station (NMS) PASS requires SNMP traps enabled (<trapenable> in <snmpd>). Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.1.2 Ensure SNMP traps is enabled

remediation.command:
GUI: Services > SNMP > SNMP Traps: tick Enable the SNMP Trap, Save.
# CIS guidance:
IN GUI:
-
Navigate to Services > SNMP.
- set checkbox "SNMP Traps Enable".
- CLIck on Save

title: Ensure that the add-on package NET-SNMP is installed and configured securely
description: The add-on package NET-SNMP provides Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) functionality on pfSense. SNMP is used for network management and monitoring, allowing administrators to collect and view information about devices on the network. This rule ensures that the NET-SNMP package is installed and securely configured.
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.1.3 Ensure that the add-on package NET-SNMP is installed and configured securely

audit.command: System > Package Manager > Installed Packages: confirm NET-SNMP is installed. In Services > SNMP (NET-SNMP) confirm SNMPv3 users use SHA authentication and AES privacy, access is restricted to authorised manager hosts, and no default community strings (public/private) remain.

remediation.command: Install NET-SNMP from System > Package Manager > Available Packages. Configure SNMPv3 users with SHA authentication and AES privacy, restrict access to the management hosts, and remove or change any default community strings. Disable the built-in bsnmpd service if it is not needed.

title: Ensure 'DNSSEC' is Enable on DNS Service
description: Enable the "DNSSEC" in the DNS Service Configuration. PASS requires DNSSEC support enabled in the DNS Resolver (<dnssec> in <unbound>). Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.3.1 Ensure 'DNSSEC' is Enable on DNS Service

remediation.command:
GUI: Services > DNS Resolver > General Settings: tick DNSSEC, Save, Apply.
# CIS guidance:
In the GUI:
-
Navigate to Services > DNS Resolver > General DNS Resolver Options
- Check the box next to 'DNSSEC' and set Enable
- CLIck 'Save'

title: Apply a Trusted Signed Certificate for VPN Portal
description: Apply a signed certificate from a trusted Certificate Authority (CA) to the SSL VPN portal to allow users to connect securely with confidence.
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.4.2 Apply a Trusted Signed Certificate for VPN Portal

audit.command: In GUI: - Navigate to System > Cert. Manager > CAs - Check the 'Issuer' Column

remediation.command:
In GUI:
-
Navigate to System > Cert. Manager > CAs
- CLIck "Add"
- In "Method" use the 'Import an existing Certificate Authority'
- Fill Textbox and Hit save.

title: Ensure that OpenVPN use strong ciphers or hashing algorithms
description: This rule aims to prevent the use of weak cryptographic algorithms in OpenVPN, which could be exploited by attackers to compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the VPN traffic. Specifically, this rule requires that only strong and secure cryptographic ciphers and hashing algorithms are used in OpenVPN.
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.5.1 Ensure that OpenVPN use strong ciphers or hashing algorithms

audit.command: VPN > OpenVPN > Servers/Clients > edit each instance: confirm Data Encryption Algorithms list only AES-256-GCM / AES-128-GCM / CHACHA20-POLY1305 (no BF-CBC, DES or other weak ciphers), Fallback Data Encryption Algorithm is AES-256-CBC or better, and Auth digest algorithm is SHA256 or stronger.

remediation.command: VPN > OpenVPN > Servers (and Clients) > edit: set Data Encryption Algorithms to AES-256-GCM and AES-128-GCM (optionally CHACHA20-POLY1305), Fallback Data Encryption Algorithm to AES-256-CBC, Auth digest algorithm to SHA256 or SHA512, Save. Update client exports.

title: Ensure syslog is configured
description: Syslog logging is a standard logging protocol that is widely supported. It is recommended for a level 1 deployment only, as syslog does not support encryption PASS requires remote logging enabled (<enable> in <syslog>) with a non-empty <remoteserver>. Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 6.1 Ensure syslog is configured

remediation.command:
GUI: Status > System Logs > Settings > Remote Logging Options: tick Enable Remote Logging, set Remote log servers, select the log contents, Save.
# CIS guidance:
In GUI:
-
Navigate to Status > System Logs > Settings.
- Configure 'Enable Remote Logging' Options

title: Ensure the WebGUI HTTP to HTTPS redirect is not disabled
description: The <disablehttpredirect> flag stops port 80 from redirecting to HTTPS. FAILs when the element is present. Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark - WebGUI - WebGUI redirect (verify section number for your pfSense release)

remediation.command: GUI: System > Advanced > Admin Access > WebGUI redirect: clear Disable webConfigurator redirect rule, Save.

title: Ensure the HTTP_REFERER check is not disabled
description: The referer check mitigates cross-site request forgery against the WebGUI. FAILs when <nohttpreferercheck> is present. Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark - WebGUI - Browser HTTP_REFERER enforcement (verify section number for your pfSense release)

remediation.command: GUI: System > Advanced > Admin Access > Browser HTTP_REFERER enforcement: clear Disable HTTP_REFERER enforcement check, Save.

title: Ensure SSH warning banner is configured
description: Before authentication is allowed, a file containing its contents must be provided to the remote user, as specified by the Banner argument.
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.1 Ensure SSH warning banner is configured

audit.command: From the pfSense shell (Diagnostics > Command Prompt or SSH option 8) run: grep '^Banner' /etc/ssh/sshd_config. A Banner line (for example Banner /etc/issue.net) must be present.

remediation.command:
In the CLI:
Edit the /etc/ssh/sshd_config file to set the parameter as follows:
Banner /etc/issue.net

title: Ensure AutoConfigBackup is enable
description: Making a backup before and after each large change or series of changes, as well as after each little change, is the recommended practice. A first backup is typically prepared in case the change being done has unfavorable repercussions.
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.2 Ensure AutoConfigBackup is enable

audit.command: Services > Auto Config Backup > Settings: confirm Enable ACB is ticked, an encryption password is set and backups are listed under the Restore tab.

remediation.command:
In the GUI.
-
Navigate to Services > Auto Config Backup.
- CLIck the Setting at the top.
- Check on the Enable ACB.
- CLIck Save

title: Ensure 'Message Of The Day (MOTD)' is set
description: Sets the MOTD message.
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.3 Ensure 'Message Of The Day (MOTD)' is set

audit.command: From the pfSense shell run: cat /etc/motd. Confirm it contains the organisation's approved message of the day instead of the FreeBSD default text.

remediation.command:
In pfSense Shell:
Type 'Message Of The Day (MOTD)' message here vi /etc/motd

title: Ensure Hostname is set
description: Changes the device default hostname. FAILs if the system hostname is still the default 'pfSense'. Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.4 Ensure Hostname is set

remediation.command:
GUI: System > General Setup > Hostname = <site-fw01>, Save.
# CIS guidance:
In the GUI:
-
Navigate to System > General Setup
- Update the field 'Hostname' with the new hostname, and CLIck "Save"

title: Ensure DNS server is configured
description: You must specify the main DNS server for your system in order to enable DNS lookups. Additionally, supplementary and third-party DNS servers can be specified. The system uses the main name server to resolve host names. The system examines the secondary name server, and if required, the tertiary, if a failure or time-out occurs. PASS requires at least one non-empty <dnsserver> in <system>. Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.5 Ensure DNS server is configured

remediation.command:
GUI: System > General Setup > DNS Server Settings: add the organisation's DNS servers, Save.
# CIS guidance:
In the GUI:
-
Navigate to System > General Setup
- Update the field DNS Servers' with the Your DNS Server, and CLIck "Save"

title: Ensure time zone is properly configured
description: Sets the local time zone information so that the device's time display is more accurate for viewers.
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 5.2.1 Ensure time zone is properly configured

audit.command: System > General Setup: confirm Timezone matches the organisation's standard and Timeservers lists approved NTP servers. Services > NTP: confirm the NTP service is enabled (the CIS audit checks Enable NTP Server).

remediation.command:
In the GUI:
-
Navigate to Services > NTP
- Checked the 'Enable NTP Server' Field
- CLIck 'Save'

title: Ensure login page autocomplete is disabled
description: Browser autocomplete stores administrator credentials on the workstation. FAILs when <loginautocomplete> is present. Audited against the pfSense config.xml (Diagnostics > Backup & Restore > Download configuration, or /cf/conf/config.xml).
reference: CIS pfSense Firewall Benchmark - WebGUI - Login Autocomplete (verify section number for your pfSense release)

remediation.command: GUI: System > Advanced > Admin Access > Login Autocomplete: clear Enable webConfigurator login autocomplete, Save.
